findings.finding: Xenomoon now diverges from xenodot on more than identity: renamed roster (product-owner), fork-only tools (mcp__ui__epic), fork-only skills (grill, xeno-epic), fork-only process docs (skill-writing). No systematic check that these divergent surfaces are wired everywhere xenodot's originals were (hooks matchers, skill-catalog derivations, templates, first-boot copy, /sync-upstream seam list) — each landed by hand-grep. Add the fork-divergent surfaces to docs/fork/SEAMS.md so /sync-upstream and the audit suite treat them as first-class seams instead of rediscovering them per session. FIRST LIVE BITE (2026-07-30, fixed 376c614): trunk tracked plugin/library/sources/skill-sources.md — a path webapp-pack installs WRITE untracked — breaking `xenomoon update` in every bound clone; invariant extracted: the trunk never tracks a path a domain-pack install writes (audit should CHECK trunk-tracked paths against every pack's install file list).
findings.pattern: every fork-divergent surface is a named seam in SEAMS.md — sync and audit read the list, not the diff.

findings.finding: agent-report/SKILL.md:31 contracts the relayed result to '<path> — gate PASS|FAIL' but nothing enforces it — no SubagentStop hook anywhere (verified 2026-07-08); review measured ~1.2k-char avg prose results vs the ~50-char contract; harden: SubagentStop regex validator + digest cap ≤6 lines (review P0B-3 merged schema).

RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-17: confirmed and WIDENING. Shipped plugin/commands/token-audit.md 1715w vs forge-local .claude/commands/token-audit.md 2309w; shipped still carries an old `## Never` while the forge-local gained `## Domain separation` + `## Do this`, and forge-local advanced again in f727444 (the jq stub gate) while shipped last moved in 51b9adf. The drift is STRUCTURAL, not accidental: the forge-local copy is the one that actually runs during an audit, so it gets improved; the shipped copy is only ever touched incidentally. DECISIVE EVIDENCE the row previously missed — the shipped copy is not merely stale, it is HARMFUL: it points the agent at `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/library/token-audits/LEDGER.md` (line 30), a CORE-TRACKED file that ships to every install, so a bound project running /token-audit appends ITS session findings into the framework's shipped library (D2 contamination by construction). It also lacks the entire `npm run token-history` / history.json half, which is forge-local anyway — so a project can only half-run the loop. RECOMMEND: delete the shipped copy; the token audit is a forge-local practice with a forge-local CLI and store. Alternative if it must ship: repoint its ledger at a PROJECT-local path and generate it from the forge-local source.
findings.pattern: a command SHIPS only if its whole loop ships — a port that loses its CLI and writes into the shipped library is worse than not shipping it.

findings.finding: The fork never pulled upstream 4a8b815 (`fix: keep subagents alive across browser disconnects`) or the 01e72a6 session refactor — `git log --all` shows ui/server/core/{registry,connection}.js have NO history here. So handleClose (session.js:306-312) calls inbox.close() + abort.abort(): a backgrounded tab, a laptop sleep or a network blip ABORTS the session and kills every in-flight sub-agent, and the reconnect builds a fresh inbox that cannot drain the old queue. Upstream instead DETACHES — swappable socket, outgoing messages buffered for replay (MAX_DETACHED_BUFFER), teardown only after 75s of IDLE and never while a turn or sub-agent runs (connection.js:53-63,154,195). Surfaced 2026-08-14 while hunting the Hermes no-ack bug; it was NOT that bug's cause (that was a degraded 21h-old process) but it is a real standing defect. Decide: port registry.js + connection.js + the onSessionId/onBusyChange hooks, or accept losing in-flight work on every blip. RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-17: all premises hold — `git log --all` returns ZERO commits for ui/server/core/{registry,connection}.js and both files are absent; handleClose still carries both inbox.close() and abort.abort(); upstream 4a8b815 is present there. PORT SIZE now measured: registry.js + connection.js = 286 LOC upstream, plus the onSessionId/onBusyChange hooks in stream.js (our copy has neither parameter). Measurement note: count via `rtk proxy`, not `rtk … | wc -l` — the wrapper's own status line inflated this by one on the first pass.
findings.pattern: an upstream FIX we never pulled is a silent regression — the sync surface should track upstream fixes, not only conflicts.

findings.finding: The webapp pack's commit gate verifies a STICKER, not the artifact. commit-gate.sh:35-44 reads `gh issue view <N> --json labels` and allows the commit when qa:pass + review:pass are present — there is NO SHA anywhere in the hook, so the pass is bound to the ISSUE, never to the code being committed. Run /qa green at SHA A, then make three more commits citing (#N): every one is allowed and none is re-verified, so the guarantee decays with each commit. tester.md:70-72 closes the loop the wrong way — once qa:pass exists the tester 'post nothing and report already QA'd — skipped' unless forced, so the first green FREEZES into a permanent pass that cannot self-correct. Net effect: the gate blocks correct code over missing paperwork and passes broken code carrying correct paperwork (observed live on a bound project: main red at root validate while every label was in order). FIX (bind the pass to the artifact, do NOT add another checker): the tester records the SHA it actually validated (qa:pass + a `qa-verified: <sha>` comment), commit-gate requires that SHA to be the parent of the commit and otherwise denies with 'verified at <a>, committing on <b> — re-run /qa', and tester idempotency keys on the SHA instead of the label's existence so a later commit re-verifies automatically. Same hook, same boundary; it just stops trusting a sticker.
findings.pattern: a gate asserts a property of the ARTIFACT (this SHA passed), never the existence of a label — a check whose failure is cleared by relabelling is a checkpoint, not a quality control.

findings.finding: Nothing carries the human's OBJECTIVE across turns, so each turn re-derives its goal from the freshest thing in context. Observed live: 'close these issues' drifted to fix deploy -> fix gate -> fix red main -> reconcile branches, ending with 3 new PRs + 1 framework issue while open issues moved 24 -> 20. NOT a missing rule: ui/orchestrator-spine.md:73-74 already says 'Never silently expand scope … a change broader than the agreed slice → stop' and :15 says 'cut ONE small slice' — the prohibition exists and was violated, so restating it harder is the label-for-a-label move (cf. D8-qa-pass-not-bound-to-sha). The MECHANISM gap is precise: the only thing in the framework that holds an objective is Autonomous Mode (standing Main Goal in .xenomoon/autonomous.json, with check turns that RESTATE the goal every tick — autonomous-main-goal/SKILL.md:9), and it is heavyweight (must be armed, self-drives, and escalates permissions via session.autonomousActive). For a plain ask there is no lightweight equivalent. Precedent for the shape of a fix already exists in the spine: it has restate-discipline for EXECUTION SHAPE ('after a correction, restate the shape in one line before dispatching anything else') but nothing for OBJECTIVE. SECOND HALF: nothing anywhere measures CLOSURE — every loop we ship counts production (tasks created, promotions filed, findings logged, epics charted), so the generated-vs-closed ratio is invisible to every mechanism in the repo, and what is not measured does not get optimised. The fix is NOT another rule and NOT a fourth subsystem beside Autonomous/epics/Pulse — reaching for a new mechanism here would enact the very failure. Design first, like Pulse got. Candidate for the closure half only: a note-class Pulse check (see D9-pulse-amplifies-scope-drift) firing on a worsening ratio, since that is deterministic state over time and fits machinery that already exists.
findings.pattern: an objective the human stated is durable and restated before each dispatch — a prohibition against drifting is not a mechanism for holding the aim.

findings.finding: HYPOTHESIS, not a measurement — Pulse (02be9c9) has never run in a live armed session yet, and this must be judged from a real one before acting. The risk: Pulse is a LEAD GENERATOR. Every beat hands the orchestrator a fresh list of things that are not done, and its first live run surfaced exactly the items a scope-drift post-mortem got lost fixing (pr:273:blocked, pr:269:blocked). Given an orchestrator that converts discovery into new work (D6-objective-not-durable), a periodic injector of new discoveries may amplify the drift it was never meant to touch. The only thing standing against that today is PROSE — the spine's Pulse rule ('Reconcile only … no code, no refactor, no new slices') plus the same sentence in the beat turn. This session's own evidence says prose guards are weak: the terse rule was stated five different ways across 14 agents, two of them runtime loads that could silently never happen. Watch on the first armed session: does a beat terminate in landing/ask-filing, or does it spawn slices? If it spawns, make the guard mechanical rather than louder — e.g. a Pulse-turn tool envelope, or beats that carry only `act`/`ask` items and drop `note` entirely when the session already has open work. Related: the closure-metric idea from D6 would live here as a note-class check, and must not itself become a to-do generator.
findings.pattern: a mechanism that surfaces work must be judged on whether it ENDS work — a safety net that adds leads faster than they close is a fuel line.

findings.finding: ui/orchestrator-spine.md:3-5 states 'This is not advisory: the session DENIES main-loop Edit/Write, MUTATING GIT, and generic catch-all agents.' No such deny exists. plugin/hooks/block-destructive-git.sh:6-8 blocks only reset|checkout|restore|stash|clean and its own header explicitly ALLOWS 'status diff log show add commit push pull fetch SWITCH branch' — and it makes NO role distinction (its :3 says it applies to subagents AND the main session), so `git switch`, `merge`, `branch -D`, `commit` and `push` are all available to the orchestrator by design. The webapp pack's push-gate/commit-gate cover push+commit, but they are PACK files: the expo pack ships no hooks at all, so in an expo-bound clone the orchestrator has unrestricted mutating git while the spine tells it it does not. This is the exact mechanism a live post-mortem identified — 'affordances beat recalled rules under load': Bash is in the toolset so `git switch` is VISIBLE, while the prohibition must be RECALLED, which is why the orchestrator could state 'I don't mutate' and then violate it a dozen times in one session, colliding with the very agents it was coordinating. FIX (CORE, not a pack — this is ROLE doctrine, not pipeline doctrine): a hook that denies MUTATING git from the MAIN LOOP ONLY (agent_id absent — push-gate.sh:16 already demonstrates the role test), naming the sanctioned path in the denial: issuekit verbs for PR/branch plumbing, a dispatch for anything else, an isolated worktree for real conflict work. Sub-agents keep their current freedom (the developer legitimately does git surgery in a worktree) and READ-ONLY git stays allowed for the orchestrator, since investigation IS its job. NUANCE that must survive the fix: the expo orchestrator deliberately routes PR plumbing to 'ONE issuekit Bash call by YOU — NEVER an agent dispatch', so the hook must ALLOW issuekit from the main loop while denying raw git — the line is ROLE (who owns this work), not RISK (does it change bytes). Either enforce the claim or stop making it; a doctrine sentence asserting a gate that does not run is the same class as D8-qa-pass-not-bound-to-sha.
findings.pattern: a prohibition the model must RECALL loses to an affordance it can SEE — enforce the role at the tool boundary, or delete the sentence claiming it is enforced.
